metrics.label: Brent crude
metrics.blurb: The global benchmark price for crude oil. Most oil cargoes price off it.

metrics.label: WTI crude
metrics.blurb: The US crude benchmark. Its gap to Brent drives US export volumes.

metrics.label: Dutch TTF gas
metrics.blurb: Europe's benchmark gas price, set in the Netherlands.
metrics.fallback: read from the daily European gas report

metrics.label: Henry Hub gas
metrics.blurb: The US benchmark gas price, set in Louisiana.

metrics.label: Coal API2 (ARA)
metrics.blurb: Price of coal delivered into northwest Europe. A dry bulk demand signal.
metrics.no_free_source: API2 coal is an Argus/McCloskey assessment and is not published free.

metrics.label: Heating oil / gasoil
metrics.blurb: A refined product price that tracks what bunker fuel costs.
metrics.no_free_source: Refined product futures are exchange-licensed; no free daily source.

metrics.label: RBOB gasoline
metrics.blurb: US gasoline price. Strong margins here pull product tankers west.
metrics.no_free_source: Refined product futures are exchange-licensed; no free daily source.

metrics.label: Dry bulk ETF (BDRY)
metrics.blurb: An ETF holding dry bulk freight futures. A rough daily read on bulker sentiment.
metrics.no_free_source: ETF quotes need an equity data provider; none is free from a server.

metrics.label: Tanker ETF (BWET)
metrics.blurb: An ETF holding tanker freight futures. A rough daily read on tanker sentiment.
metrics.no_free_source: ETF quotes need an equity data provider; none is free from a server.

metrics.label: Baltic Capesize Index
metrics.blurb: The Capesize component of the Baltic Dry Index. The most volatile part, and effectively a bet on Chinese steel production.

metrics.label: Baltic Panamax Index
metrics.blurb: The Panamax component. Coal and grain rather than iron ore, so it follows harvests and power demand more than steel.

metrics.label: Baltic Supramax Index
metrics.blurb: The Supramax component. These ships have their own cranes and serve smaller ports, so it reflects broad trade rather than one commodity.

metrics.label: Baltic Dry Index
metrics.blurb: The Baltic Exchange's headline dry bulk freight index. Published late afternoon London time, so a morning brief shows the previous session.
metrics.source: Baltic Exchange via Hellenic Shipping News

metrics.label: VLSFO Singapore
metrics.blurb: Price of the main low-sulphur marine fuel at the world's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Rotterdam
metrics.blurb: The same fuel in Europe's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Fujairah
metrics.blurb: The Middle East bunker hub, where most VLCC voyages refuel.

metrics.label: Diesel crack vs Brent
metrics.blurb: Roughly what a refinery makes turning a barrel of crude into diesel. Computed as the gasoil price converted to barrels minus Brent. Fat margins make refineries run hard, which creates product tanker cargo.

metrics.label: Brent–WTI spread
metrics.blurb: How much more Brent costs than WTI. A wide gap makes exporting US crude profitable, which means more long-haul cargoes and stronger tanker demand.

rates.label: VLCC (TD3C, AG→China)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a 2m-barrel crude tanker on the Arabian Gulf to China run. The most quoted tanker rate in the world.

rates.label: Suezmax (TD20, W.Africa→UKC)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a 1m-barrel crude tanker from West Africa to Europe.

rates.label: Aframax (TD7, N.Sea→UKC)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a 600k-barrel crude tanker on a short North Sea haul — the route closest to Norwegian crude exports.

rates.label: LR2 (TC1, AG→Japan)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a large product tanker carrying clean refined products.

rates.label: MR (TC2, Rotterdam→NY)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a mid-size product tanker on the transatlantic gasoline run.

rates.label: MR (TC14, US Gulf→UKC)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a mid-size product tanker carrying clean products east across the Atlantic.

rates.label: Capesize 5TC
rates.blurb: Average daily earnings of a 180,000t bulker across five iron ore and coal routes.

rates.label: Panamax 4TC
rates.blurb: Average daily earnings of an 82,000t bulker, mostly coal and grain.
rates.why_unavailable: Not quoted in the latest published market report. The Baltic assessment itself is a paid product; this row fills whenever the figure appears in the public commentary.

rates.label: Supramax 10TC
rates.blurb: Average daily earnings of a 58,000t geared bulker across ten routes.
rates.why_unavailable: Not quoted in the latest published market report. The Baltic assessment itself is a paid product; this row fills whenever the figure appears in the public commentary.

rates.label: Handysize 7TC
rates.blurb: Average daily earnings of a 38,000t bulker, the smallest Baltic-assessed class.
rates.why_unavailable: Not quoted in the latest published market report. The Baltic assessment itself is a paid product; this row fills whenever the figure appears in the public commentary.

rates.label: LNG (BLNG1, Australia→Japan)
rates.blurb: Spot charter rate for a standard LNG carrier on the Pacific route.

rates.label: LNG (BLNG2, US Gulf→Continent)
rates.blurb: The Atlantic LNG route. US cargoes to Europe are the short haul; compare with BLNG3 to see which way cargoes are being pulled.

rates.label: LNG (BLNG3, US Gulf→Japan)
rates.blurb: The long-haul LNG route. It pays more than BLNG2 because the voyage is far longer, so the gap between them tracks the TTF–JKM arbitrage.

rates.label: VLGC (BLPG1, Ras Tanura→Chiba)
rates.blurb: Daily earnings of a very large gas carrier moving LPG from the Gulf to Japan.
